# Data import
```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(here)
library(lubridate)
library(maps)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)

keep <- c("TIMESTAMP_START", "TIMESTAMP_END", "TA_F", "SW_IN_F", "VPD_F", "P_F",
          "NETRAD", "G_F_MDS", "H_F_MDS", "H_F_MDS_QC", "LE_F_MDS", "LE_F_MDS_QC",
          "NEE_VUT_REF", "NEE_VUT_REF_QC", "GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "RECO_NT_VUT_REF")

read_hh <- function(zip_file) {
  # find the half-hourly FLUXMET file inside this zip
  hh_name <- grep("FLUXMET_HH", unzip(zip_file, list = TRUE)$Name, value = TRUE)[1]
  # unzip only that csv
  unzip(zip_file, files = hh_name, exdir = "data/raw/unzipped", overwrite = T)
  # read it
  hh <- read_csv(file.path("data/raw/unzipped", hh_name),
               na = "-9999",
               col_select = any_of(keep),
               col_types = cols(TIMESTAMP_START = "c", TIMESTAMP_END = "c", .default = "d"))
  hh$site <- str_extract(basename(hh_name), "[A-Z]{2}-[A-Za-z0-9]+") # add site id from file name
  return(hh)} # return clean table

zip_files <- list.files(here("data", "raw"), pattern = "\\.zip$", full.names = TRUE)

flux <- map_dfr(zip_files, read_hh) # apply the functiont to each one and combine results
flux <- flux |> mutate(time = as.POSIXct(TIMESTAMP_START, format = "%Y%m%d%H%M", tz = "UTC"))
flux[flux == -9999] <- NA
```

# C1. Site overview
```{r}
#| label: site overview
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

# inspect snapshot
snapshot_file <- list.files(here("data", "snapshots"), pattern = "fluxnet_shuttle_snapshot_.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)[1]
snapshot <- read_csv(snapshot_file)

names(snapshot)

site_overview <- snapshot |>
  filter(site_id %in% unique(flux$site)) |>
  select(site_id, site_name, data_hub, igbp, location_lat, location_long, 
  first_year, last_year, product_citation) |>
    mutate(country = case_when(
      site_id == "US-Myb" ~ "United States",
      site_id == "CN-Dmn" ~ "China",
      site_id == "CH-Cha" ~ "Switzerland",
      site_id == "FR-Bil" ~ "France",
      site_id == "AU-Cum" ~ "Australia")) |>
    relocate(country, .after = site_name)

site_overview

world <- map_data("world")

ggplot() +  
    geom_polygon(data = world, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group), fill = "grey90", colour = "white") +
    geom_point(data = site_overview, aes(x = location_long, y = location_lat), colour = "red", size = 3) +
    geom_text(data = site_overview, aes(x = location_long, y = location_lat, label = site_id), vjust = -1, size = 3) +
    coord_quickmap() +
    labs(x = "Longitude (°)", y = "Latitude (°)", title = "Locations of my five FLUXNET towers") +
    theme_minimal()
```

# C2. Data coverage
```{r}
#| label: data-coverage
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

coverage <- flux |>
  mutate(year = year(time)) |>
  group_by(site, year) |>
  summarise(share_measured = mean(NEE_VUT_REF_QC == 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(coverage, aes(x = year, y = site, fill = share_measured)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Share of NEE measured", labels = scales::percent, option = "viridis") +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Site", title = "Share of half-hourly NEE measurements by site and year") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The best-covered NEE data are generally found in the years 2015-2024. The first year has mostly bad coverage. CH-Cha has the worst NEE data coverage and AU-Cum the best.

# C3. Summary statistics
```{r}
vars_to_summarize <- c("TA_F", "SW_IN_F", "VPD_F", "P_F", "NEE_VUT_REF", 
                       "GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "RECO_NT_VUT_REF", "H_F_MDS", "LE_F_MDS")

units <- c("TA_F" = "°C", "SW_IN_F" = "W m⁻²", "VPD_F" = "kPa", "P_F" = "mm yr⁻¹", 
           "NEE_VUT_REF" = "µmol m⁻² s⁻¹", "GPP_NT_VUT_REF" = "µmol m⁻² s⁻¹", 
           "RECO_NT_VUT_REF" = "µmol m⁻² s⁻¹", "H_F_MDS" = "W m⁻²", "LE_F_MDS" = "W m⁻²")

summary_table <- flux |>
  select(site, all_of(vars_to_summarize)) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -site, names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  filter(variable != "P_F") |> # Exclude P_F here
  group_by(site, variable) |>
  summarise(
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    perc_missing = mean(is.na(value)) * 100,
    .groups = "drop")

# Precipitation as Mean Annual Sum
precip_stats <- flux |>
  mutate(year = year(time)) |>
  group_by(site, year) |>
  summarise(annual_sum = sum(P_F, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(
    variable = "P_F",
    mean = mean(annual_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(annual_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(annual_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
    perc_missing = (sum(is.na(flux$P_F[flux$site == first(site)])) / length(flux$P_F[flux$site == first(site)])) * 100,
    .groups = "drop")

summary_combined <- bind_rows(summary_table, precip_stats)

# create variable_unit column
summary_final <- summary_combined |>
  mutate(variable_unit = paste0(variable, " (", units[variable], ")")) |>
  select(site, variable_unit, mean, min, max, perc_missing)

site_list <- unique(flux$site)
for (s in site_list) {
    cat("\n### Site:", s, "\n")
    print(knitr::kable(summary_final |> filter(site == s) |> select(-site)))}
```

# C4. Time series
```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

# half-hourly data to daily values
daily_flux <- flux |>
  mutate(date = as_date(time)) |> 
  group_by(site, date) |>
  summarise(
    NEE = mean(NEE_VUT_REF, na.rm = TRUE),
    GPP = mean(GPP_NT_VUT_REF, na.rm = TRUE),
    RECO = mean(RECO_NT_VUT_REF, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop")

conv_factor <- 1.0378

daily_flux_conv <- daily_flux |>
  mutate(across(c(NEE, GPP, RECO), ~ .x * conv_factor))

plot_data <- daily_flux_conv |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(NEE, GPP, RECO), 
               names_to = "Flux_Type", 
               values_to = "Value")

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = date, y = Value, color = Flux_Type)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~site, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("GPP" = "forestgreen", "RECO" = "brown", "NEE" = "black")) +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Carbon Fluxes per Site",
    x = "Date",
    y = expression("Flux (g C m^-2 d^-1)"),
    color = "Flux Type") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# C5. Diurnal cycles
```{r}
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: 10

# Join latitude info to the flux data for hemisphere
flux_with_lat <- flux |>
  left_join(site_overview |> select(site_id, location_lat), by = c("site" = "site_id"))

# Hour and Month variables
flux_with_time <- flux_with_lat |>
  mutate(hour = hour(time), month = month(time))

# Define seasons based on hemisphere and month
# Northern: DJF=Winter, MAM=Spring, JJA=Summer, SON=Autumn
# Southern: DJF=Summer, MAM=Autumn, JJA=Winter, SON=Spring
flux_with_seasons <- flux_with_time |>
  mutate(season = case_when(
    location_lat >= 0 & month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter",
    location_lat >= 0 & month %in% c(3, 4, 5)  ~ "Spring",
    location_lat >= 0 & month %in% c(6, 7, 8)  ~ "Summer",
    location_lat >= 0 & month %in% c(9, 10, 11) ~ "Autumn",
    location_lat < 0  & month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Summer",
    location_lat < 0  & month %in% c(3, 4, 5)  ~ "Autumn",
    location_lat < 0  & month %in% c(6, 7, 8)  ~ "Winter",
    location_lat < 0  & month %in% c(9, 10, 11) ~ "Spring"))

diurnal_summary <- flux_with_seasons |>
  group_by(site, season, hour) |>
  summarise(NEE = mean(NEE_VUT_REF, na.rm = TRUE), LE = mean(LE_F_MDS, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(NEE, LE), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value")

ggplot(diurnal_summary, aes(x = hour, y = Value, color = site)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  facet_grid(Variable ~ season, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Diurnal Course of NEE and LE: Comparison across Sites", x = "Hour of Day (UTC)", y = "Mean Value",
    color = "Tower Site") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, 3)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"), 
  panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines"))
```

To determine the seasons, I used the latitude of each tower. For sites in the Northern Hemisphere (latitude ≥0), I assigned December, January, and February as Winter. For the site in the Southern Hemisphere (latitude <0), I reversed the seasonal assignment, designating December, January, and February as Summer. The diurnal cycles were then calculated by averaging all observations for each hour of the day across the respective seasons.

# C6. Your reading (energy balance)
```{r}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 5

# Find a site that has both NETRAD and G_F_MDS (check for fewest NAs for these variables)
energy_check <- flux |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(valid_data = sum(!is.na(NETRAD) & !is.na(G_F_MDS))) |>
  arrange(desc(valid_data))

best_site <- energy_check$site[1] # pick site with the most data

# prepare data for scatter plot
eb_data <- flux |>
  filter(site == best_site) |>
  filter(H_F_MDS_QC == 0 & LE_F_MDS_QC == 0) |> # only measured H and LE
  mutate(available_energy = NETRAD - G_F_MDS, turbulent_energy = H_F_MDS + LE_F_MDS) |>
  filter(!is.na(available_energy), !is.na(turbulent_energy))

# linear fit for the slope
fit <- lm(turbulent_energy ~ available_energy, data = eb_data)
slope_val <- round(coef(fit)[2], 3)

ggplot(eb_data, aes(x = available_energy, y = turbulent_energy)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.5, color = "grey50") +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "red", linewidth = 1) + # 1:1 line
  geom_abline(intercept = coef(fit)[1], slope = coef(fit)[2], color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = paste("Energy Balance for site", best_site),
    subtitle = paste("Red = 1:1 line | Blue = Linear fit (Slope:", slope_val, ")"),
    x = expression("Available Energy (NETRAD" - "G_F_MDS) [W m^-2]"),
    y = expression("Turbulent Energy (H_F_MDS" + "LE_F_MDS) [W m^-2]")) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Comparing the five towers, CN-Dmn takes up the most carbon per year, as seen by its consistently lower NEE values in the daily time series. The largest seasonal cycle was also observed at CN-Dmn, where the flux shifted the strongest between the growing and non-growing seasons. I was surprised by how much the data quality varies between the sites. The share of measured NEE was highest for AU-Cum, while CH-Cha had significant gaps, meaning a large proportion of their annual totals are based on gap-filled estimates rather than direct measurements.
